themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: Focuses on AI agents performing research tasks autonomously or with minimal human intervention, including tasks like data analysis, literature reviews, and scientific discovery.

themes.name: AI research tools
themes.description: Covers a broad range of AI-powered tools specifically designed to aid in various research processes, from data collection and analysis to literature discovery and synthesis.

themes.name: AI summarization
themes.description: Articles discussing AI's ability to condense large amounts of text, such as meeting transcripts, research papers, or earnings calls, into concise summaries.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Focuses on AI tools that assist developers in writing, debugging, reviewing, and optimizing code.

themes.name: Synthetic users
themes.description: Explores the creation and use of simulated users or personas for testing and research purposes, often leveraging AI to generate realistic behaviors or data.

themes.name: AI usability testing
themes.description: Covers the application of AI in automating or augmenting the process of evaluating the usability of products and interfaces.

themes.name: AI design research
themes.description: Examines how AI is being used to inform and enhance the design process, from user research to ideation and prototyping.

themes.name: AI customer insights
themes.description: Articles focused on AI's role in extracting and analyzing customer data to generate actionable insights for product and business strategies.

themes.name: AI for product management
themes.description: Discusses how AI tools and techniques are applied to various aspects of product management, including strategy, development, and user feedback analysis.

themes.name: AI qualitative research
themes.description: Covers the use of AI in analyzing and understanding qualitative data, such as interview transcripts or open-ended survey responses.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
